0.name: Diffusion Transformer Quantization and Sparsity
0.one_line: These papers speed up image and video diffusion transformers with post-training or quantization-aware quantization and trainable sparse attention.

1.name: LLM Benchmarking and LLM-as-a-Judge
1.one_line: These papers study how LLMs are evaluated, covering benchmark design and reliability, judge bias, leaderboard rankings and AI peer review.

2.name: Long-Context Sparse and Linear Attention
2.one_line: These papers make long-context language models efficient through sparse attention, linear RNNs and state-space models, and positional encodings that extend context length.

3.name: Reward Models and Human Behavior Modeling
3.one_line: These papers mix reward and process-reward modeling for LLMs, including reward hacking, with computational models of human and animal decision-making behavior.

4.name: Transformer Mechanisms and Expressivity Theory
4.one_line: These papers analyze how transformers compute, covering in-context learning theory, looped transformers, attention sinks, massive activations and length generalization.

5.name: LLM Knowledge Editing and Forgetting
5.one_line: These papers update or edit the factual knowledge stored in LLMs and study the forgetting and memorization that happen during continual post-training.

6.name: Continual Learning and Catastrophic Forgetting
6.one_line: These papers learn new classes or tasks one after another without forgetting old ones, often with LoRA adapters, merging or optimizers built for stability and plasticity.

7.name: Controllable Video Generation and Editing
7.one_line: These papers generate and edit videos with control over subjects, motion, identity and lighting, often by turning image editors into video editors.

8.name: 3D Gaussian Splatting
8.one_line: These papers improve 3D Gaussian splatting and neural rendering for novel view synthesis, including feed-forward reconstruction, compression and densification.

9.name: Robustness of LLM Safety Alignment
9.one_line: These papers study how safety alignment and refusal behavior in LLMs and multimodal models hold up, break under jailbreaks or fine-tuning, and can be made more robust.

10.name: Latent and Chain-of-Thought Visual Reasoning
10.one_line: These papers improve and diagnose how vision-language models reason over images, including latent visual reasoning, visual chain-of-thought and grounding.

11.name: KV Cache Compression and Eviction
11.one_line: These papers shrink the memory cost of LLM inference by evicting, quantizing, pruning or reusing key-value cache entries.

12.name: Diffusion Language Models
12.one_line: These papers develop masked and discrete diffusion language models, focusing on parallel decoding, speculative sampling, unmasking strategies and RL post-training.

13.name: Optimal Transport Algorithms and Theory
13.one_line: These papers propose solvers and estimation theory for optimal transport, including Gromov-Wasserstein, sliced, unbalanced and barycenter problems.

14.name: Samplers and Diffusion-Based Sampling
14.one_line: These papers design and analyze samplers built on diffusion models, Langevin dynamics and sequential Monte Carlo, including posterior sampling for inverse problems.

15.name: Goal-Conditioned and Reward-Free RL
15.one_line: These papers train RL agents to reach goals or satisfy formal task specifications such as temporal logic and reward machines, often offline and with subgoal planning.

16.name: Learning with Noisy and Weak Labels
16.one_line: These papers handle imperfect supervision such as label noise, partial and positive-unlabeled labels, class imbalance and active learning, along with surrogate-loss theory.

17.name: Dexterous and Humanoid Robot Manipulation
17.one_line: These papers learn dexterous hand-object interaction, humanoid loco-manipulation and contact-rich control, often from egocentric human videos and tactile or force signals.

18.name: Policy Gradient and MDP Convergence Theory
18.one_line: These papers prove convergence and sample-complexity results for policy gradient, value iteration and off-policy evaluation in discounted and average-reward MDPs.

19.name: Cooperative Multi-Agent RL
19.one_line: These papers train teams of agents to coordinate and explore in cooperative or mixed-motive multi-agent reinforcement learning and Markov games.

20.name: Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents
20.one_line: These papers build and benchmark memory systems that let LLM agents store, retrieve and update past experience over long dialogues and tasks.

21.name: Multimodal Agents and Reasoning Benchmarks
21.one_line: These papers evaluate and train multimodal LLM agents for web search, deep research, tool use and embodied decision-making, mostly through new benchmarks.

22.name: Anomaly Detection Across Modalities
22.one_line: These papers detect anomalies in industrial images, time series, graphs, video and audio, including zero-shot and few-shot settings.

23.name: Weather, Climate and Air Quality Forecasting
23.one_line: These papers forecast weather, air quality, cyclones and other environmental and energy quantities with ML models and new benchmarks.

24.name: Efficient Image Diffusion
24.one_line: These papers make image diffusion models faster and higher-resolution through feature caching, few-step distillation, pixel-space diffusion and diffusion-based super-resolution.

25.name: Multimodal Fusion and Missing Modalities
25.one_line: These papers study how multimodal models combine modalities, addressing modality imbalance, missing modalities, cross-modal alignment and synergy.

26.name: Action-Conditioned Video World Models
26.one_line: These papers build interactive, action-conditioned video world models for robots, games and embodied agents, sometimes combined with vision-language-action policies.

27.name: Federated Learning under Heterogeneity
27.one_line: These papers train models across distributed clients with non-IID data, covering aggregation, personalization, federated LoRA, robustness and privacy.

28.name: Domain Adaptation and Generalization
28.one_line: These papers transfer models across distribution shifts through unsupervised, source-free and graph domain adaptation and domain generalization.

29.name: Treatment Effect Estimation and Causal Inference
29.one_line: These papers estimate heterogeneous and average treatment effects and counterfactual outcomes from observational, experimental and survival data.

30.name: Neural Scaling Laws for Pretraining
30.one_line: These papers fit, explain and extrapolate power-law scaling laws that relate loss to model size, data and compute, and derive compute-optimal training recipes.

31.name: Privacy Auditing and Membership Inference
31.one_line: These papers design differentially private training and accounting mechanisms, and audit privacy leakage with membership inference attacks.

32.name: LLM Agentic Reasoning Strategies
32.one_line: These papers study how language-model agents choose and combine reasoning strategies for planning, abstraction and scientific problem solving, often with new benchmarks.

33.name: Muon, Adam and Sign-Based Optimizers
33.one_line: These papers analyse and design neural-network optimizers such as Muon, Adam, Lion and SignSGD, covering orthogonalized updates, momentum and edge-of-stability dynamics.

34.name: LLM Self-Explanation and Hidden Computation
34.one_line: These papers probe what computations transformers perform internally, such as in-context learning, copying, belief states and hidden reasoning over filler tokens.

35.name: Coding Agents and SWE Benchmarks
35.one_line: These papers benchmark and train LLM coding agents on repository-level software engineering, long-horizon development and debugging tasks.

36.name: Shapley Values and Feature Attribution
36.one_line: These papers develop and critique post-hoc explanation methods such as Shapley values, integrated gradients and causal attributions for model predictions.

37.name: PAC Learning and Sample Complexity
37.one_line: These papers prove sample-complexity and lower bounds for PAC, online and agnostic learning, especially of halfspaces and concept classes with VC or Littlestone dimension.

38.name: Molecular and Materials ML
38.one_line: These papers build models and benchmarks for chemistry tasks such as reaction prediction, retrosynthesis, mass-spectrometry retrieval and machine-learned interatomic potentials.

39.name: Efficient and Long Video Diffusion
39.one_line: These papers extend video diffusion models to long or streaming generation with autoregressive rollout, memory for consistency, and distillation for real-time speed.

40.name: Graph and Hypergraph Generation
40.one_line: These papers propose diffusion, flow-matching, autoencoder and sequence models that generate graphs and hypergraphs at scale.

41.name: 3D Molecule and Material Generation
41.one_line: These papers generate 3D molecules, crystals, proteins and materials with equivariant diffusion, flow and autoregressive models, including structure-based drug design.

42.name: Video Temporal Grounding and Segmentation
42.one_line: These papers localize actions, moments and objects in time and space in video, covering temporal grounding, video object segmentation and video reasoning segmentation.

43.name: Deep Network Theory and Learning Dynamics
43.one_line: These papers analyse ReLU and residual networks theoretically, covering implicit bias, incremental learning, parameter symmetries, identifiability and feature learning.

44.name: Physics-Informed Networks and PDE Foundation Models
44.one_line: These papers solve partial differential equations with physics-informed networks, neural surrogates, PDE foundation models and generative inverse solvers.

45.name: Language-Grounded 3D Scene Understanding
45.one_line: These papers ground language in 3D scenes for open-vocabulary understanding, spatial reasoning, affordances and localization using point clouds, multi-view images and 3D-LLMs.

46.name: CLIP-Style Image-Text Alignment
46.one_line: These papers improve image-text alignment in CLIP-style and vision-language models for compositional understanding, long captions and image retrieval.

47.name: Long-Video Understanding with MLLMs
47.one_line: These papers help multimodal LLMs answer questions over long and streaming videos via frame selection, token allocation, KV-cache memory and agentic pipelines.

48.name: LLM Personas, Sycophancy and Cultural Bias
48.one_line: These papers measure how LLMs simulate personas and opinions and how they show sycophancy, stereotypes and cultural or value biases.

49.name: Machine Unlearning in LLMs
49.one_line: These papers remove the influence of specific training data from models, mainly LLMs, while preserving utility and resisting relearning.

50.name: Neural Decoding from Brain Recordings
50.one_line: These papers decode speech, images and intentions from brain recordings and build brain foundation models and datasets for brain-computer interfaces.

51.name: In-Context RL and Offline Policy Steering
51.one_line: These papers learn and adapt policies from fixed datasets, behavior foundation models and in-context RL, including safe offline RL and post-training policy steering.

52.name: Low-Bit LLM Quantization
52.one_line: These papers compress LLM weights and activations to low bit-widths through post-training quantization, quantization-aware training and mixed-precision search.

53.name: Constrained and Robust MDPs
53.one_line: These papers give provable algorithms for constrained, chance-constrained and robust Markov decision processes, often via primal-dual policy optimization.

54.name: LLM-Driven Evolutionary Design and Discovery
54.one_line: These papers use LLMs, often with evolutionary search, to formulate optimization models, discover algorithms and generate engineering or combinatorial code, with benchmarks for each.

55.name: Performative Prediction and Decision-Focused Learning
55.one_line: These papers study predictions that feed into decisions, including performative prediction, predict-then-optimize, recalibration and learning-augmented algorithms.

56.name: Sequential and Generative Recommendation
56.one_line: These papers model user preferences for sequential, multimodal and generative recommendation, increasingly with LLMs and diffusion models.

57.name: LiDAR, Radar and Multi-Sensor Perception
57.one_line: These papers handle LiDAR, radar and multi-sensor data for localization, point-cloud registration, scene flow and HD map construction in driving and UAV settings.

58.name: Spiking Neural Networks
58.one_line: These papers train and analyse spiking neural networks for energy-efficient neuromorphic computing, using learnable delays, neuron models and plasticity rules.

59.name: Clinical LLMs and Medical Benchmarks
59.one_line: These papers evaluate and build LLM agents for clinical reasoning, EHR tasks, medical QA and report generation, along with medical benchmarks.

60.name: Statistical Theory of Diffusion Models
60.one_line: Theoretical and statistical work on score-based diffusion models, density estimation, denoising and posterior inference for inverse problems.

61.name: Neural Operator Surrogates for PDEs
61.one_line: Neural operator and transformer surrogates that learn to solve partial differential equations for physical simulation and forecasting.

62.name: Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Diffusion
62.one_line: Removing unsafe concepts or styles from text-to-image diffusion models, plus adversarial attacks and defenses on vision-language models.

63.name: Part-Level 3D Asset Generation
63.one_line: Generating structured, part-decomposed or articulated 3D objects and scenes from images or text.

64.name: Differentially Private Estimation Rates
64.one_line: Algorithms and optimal rates for statistical estimation, optimization and data analysis under central or local differential privacy.

65.name: Learning Equilibria in Games
65.one_line: Learning dynamics and sample complexity for reaching Nash or correlated equilibria in zero-sum, Markov and potential games.

66.name: Latent World Models for Planning
66.one_line: Latent and symbolic world models that let robots and LLM agents predict outcomes and plan actions.

67.name: AI-Generated Image and Deepfake Detection
67.one_line: Detecting and localizing AI-generated images, deepfake videos and image tampering for media forensics.

68.name: Medical Imaging and Pathology Models
68.one_line: Segmentation, representation learning and vision-language models for radiology, CT and whole-slide pathology images.

69.name: Model Merging and LoRA Fusion
69.one_line: Combining fine-tuned models, task vectors or LoRA adapters into a single model without retraining.

70.name: Vision-Language-Action Robot Policies
70.one_line: Training, fine-tuning, analysing and evaluating vision-language-action models for robotic manipulation.

71.name: Flow Matching Theory and Variants
71.one_line: New formulations, theory and constrained or distilled variants of flow matching and transport-based generative models.

72.name: End-to-End Autonomous Driving
72.one_line: End-to-end driving planners, driving VLA models, world models and benchmarks for autonomous vehicles.

73.name: Vision Datasets, Benchmarks and Evaluation
73.one_line: Benchmarks probing multimodal models on specialised imagery such as remote sensing, medical scans, documents, try-on and image quality.

74.name: Multi-Turn LLM Dialogue and Agent RL
74.one_line: Reinforcement learning, credit assignment and evaluation for LLMs in multi-turn conversations and interactive agent tasks.

75.name: Activation Steering of LLMs
75.one_line: Controlling language model behaviour at inference time by editing internal activations with steering vectors or subspace interventions.

76.name: Self-Evolving Agents and Skill Learning
76.one_line: LLM agents that discover, store, reuse and evolve skills to solve long-horizon web, embodied and tool-use tasks.

77.name: 4D Reconstruction from Monocular Video
77.one_line: Recovering dynamic 3D geometry, motion and human or object animation from monocular or multi-view video.

78.name: RAG Faithfulness and Knowledge Conflicts
78.one_line: Improving faithfulness, efficiency, privacy and knowledge-conflict handling in retrieval-augmented LLM generation.

79.name: Test-Time and Few-Shot VLM Adaptation
79.one_line: Adapting, fine-tuning, distilling and robustifying CLIP-style vision-language models and vision transformers under distribution shift.

80.name: LLM Agent Reliability and Efficiency
80.one_line: Making LLM agents more reliable, safe and cost-efficient through tool-call decisions, failure prediction, abstention and resource control.

81.name: LLM Theorem Proving and Formal Math
81.one_line: Using LLMs for formal theorem proving in Lean, autoformalization, proof grading and math reasoning benchmarks.

82.name: Text-to-Image Generation and Evaluation
82.one_line: Improving and evaluating text-to-image models via reward models, compositional control, aesthetics and bias analysis.

83.name: LLM Multi-Agent Systems
83.one_line: Designing, training and evaluating teams of collaborating or debating LLM agents, including coordination and orchestration.

84.name: LLM-Generated GPU Kernels and Systems
84.one_line: Using LLMs and agents to write and tune CUDA or Triton kernels, plus benchmarks for HPC and ML systems code.

85.name: Watermarking Generative Model Outputs
85.one_line: Embedding and detecting watermarks in LLM text, images and audio to trace AI-generated content.

86.name: Preference Optimization for LLM Alignment
86.one_line: DPO-style and RLHF objectives, data selection and robustness methods for aligning LLMs with human preferences.

87.name: Graph Neural Networks
87.one_line: GNN architectures, graph contrastive learning, temporal graphs and graph foundation models for node, link and graph tasks.

88.name: Image Restoration and Inverse Problems
88.one_line: Denoising, super-resolution, image fusion and plug-and-play or diffusion-based restoration of degraded images.

89.name: Protein, Antibody and RNA Design
89.one_line: Generative models and optimization for designing proteins, antibodies, peptides, RNA and DNA sequences.

90.name: LoRA and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
90.one_line: Proposes low-rank, sparse, orthogonal and zeroth-order adapter variants and optimizers for fine-tuning large language models with less memory and compute.

91.name: Online Convex Optimization Regret Bounds
91.one_line: Derives regret guarantees for online convex and non-convex optimization under delays, switching costs, memory and bandit feedback.

92.name: GRPO-Style RL with Verifiable Rewards
92.one_line: Studies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for reasoning models, focusing on GRPO-style advantage estimation, rollout efficiency and training stability.

93.name: Recurrent Network Dynamics in Neuroscience
93.one_line: Analyzes learning and dynamics in low-rank RNNs, Hopfield networks and reservoirs as models of neural circuits and memory.

94.name: Diffusion Guidance and Reward Fine-Tuning
94.one_line: Improves how diffusion and flow models are guided and sampled, including classifier-free guidance, reward-guided and RL post-training, few-step generation and score-matching analysis.

95.name: Urban Mobility and Trajectory Generation
95.one_line: Generates and forecasts vehicle and human trajectories, traffic and spatio-temporal events in cities, including cross-city transfer and benchmarks.

96.name: Grokking, Memorization and Generalization Theory
96.one_line: Explains why overparameterized networks generalize, covering grokking, double descent, memorization versus generalization and compression-based bounds.

97.name: Object Detection and OOD Detection
97.one_line: Develops open-world, domain-adaptive and long-tailed object detectors and methods for detecting out-of-distribution inputs in vision models.

98.name: Multi-View Clustering and Person Re-ID
98.one_line: Learns fused representations across multiple views or modalities for multi-view clustering, incomplete multi-view learning and person or object re-identification.

99.name: Instruction-Based Image Editing
99.one_line: Builds datasets, guidance schemes and RL training for editing images from text instructions, exemplars or drag inputs while preserving unedited content.

100.name: Mechanism Design, Auctions and Social Choice
100.one_line: Designs and analyzes auctions, pricing, resource allocation, persuasion and voting rules for strategic agents, often with learning-augmented guarantees.

101.name: Conformal Prediction Coverage Guarantees
101.one_line: Constructs conformal prediction sets and intervals with marginal, conditional or online coverage guarantees under shift, grouping and multivariate outputs.

102.name: Feed-Forward Multi-View Geometry Transformers
102.one_line: Builds and accelerates feed-forward and streaming multi-view geometry transformers for 3D reconstruction, camera pose, depth and panoramic geometry estimation.

103.name: Learning Dynamical Systems from Data
103.one_line: Identifies latent and chaotic dynamical systems from observations using Koopman operators, neural ODEs/SDEs, switching models and equation discovery.

104.name: Speculative Decoding for LLM Inference
104.one_line: Speeds up LLM generation and serving with draft-and-verify speculative decoding, tree drafting, self-speculation and scheduling.

105.name: LLM Agent Safety and Security
105.one_line: Benchmarks and defends LLM, computer-use and multi-agent systems against prompt injection, unsafe actions, sabotage and scheming.

106.name: Quantum Machine Learning
106.one_line: Applies machine learning to quantum systems and studies quantum neural networks, circuits, kernels, tomography and neural quantum states.

107.name: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Models
107.one_line: Builds foundation models and generative methods for single-cell gene expression, spatial transcriptomics from histology, perturbation response and genomic sequences.

108.name: Verified Code and Software Security Benchmarks
108.one_line: Evaluates LLMs on formally verified code generation, proof writing, vulnerability detection, reverse engineering and cybersecurity tasks.

109.name: Bayesian Inference and Gaussian Processes
109.one_line: Develops variational inference, neural posterior estimation, Gaussian process and Laplace methods for scalable and robust Bayesian inference.

110.name: Amortized and LLM-Informed Causal Discovery
110.one_line: Recovers causal graphs from observational, interventional or time-series data, including amortized foundation models and LLM-informed priors.

111.name: Brain Encoding and Neural Recording Analysis
111.one_line: Models fMRI, EEG and spiking recordings with encoding models, connectivity estimation and neural data tokenizers, plus connectomics benchmarks.

112.name: Calibration and Prediction-Powered Inference
112.one_line: Studies post-hoc calibration, multicalibration and prediction-powered inference for reliable estimates and evaluation with few labels.

113.name: Jailbreak and Red-Teaming Attacks
113.one_line: Designs, scales and detects jailbreak and red-teaming attacks on LLMs, multimodal and diffusion language models, along with safety defenses.

114.name: Irregular and Continuous-Time Sequences
114.one_line: Models irregularly sampled and continuous-time sequences with neural CDEs, state-space models and point processes, often for EHR, ECG, sleep and wearable data.

115.name: Geometry of Learned Representations
115.one_line: Analyzes and designs embedding spaces using manifold, hyperbolic, Riemannian, spherical and topological structure for representation learning.

116.name: Best-Arm Identification in Bandits
116.one_line: Gives sample-complexity bounds and algorithms for fixed-confidence and fixed-budget best-arm identification and pure exploration in bandits.

117.name: Flow and Diffusion Policy Optimization
117.one_line: Trains diffusion and flow-matching policies with policy gradients, Q-guidance and offline-to-online RL for multimodal continuous control.

118.name: Retriever and Long-Document Benchmarks
118.one_line: Builds benchmarks and pipelines for retrievers, embedding models, deep search and long-document understanding with evidence grounding.

119.name: Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation
119.one_line: Builds single models and visual tokenizers that both understand and generate images, including autoregressive and representation-autoencoder approaches.

120.name: Regret Bounds for Stochastic and Contextual Bandits
120.one_line: Regret bounds and algorithms for stochastic, linear, contextual, dueling and cascading bandit problems.

121.name: Generative Policies for Offline RL
121.one_line: Offline and offline-to-online reinforcement learning using diffusion, flow-matching and generative policies trained on fixed datasets.

122.name: Embodied Spatial Reasoning in VLMs
122.one_line: Benchmarks and agentic methods for 3D and embodied spatial reasoning in vision-language models.

123.name: Deep RL Representations and Multitask
123.one_line: General deep reinforcement learning methods covering representation learning, multitask, meta, transfer, safe and model-based RL.

124.name: LLM Pruning and MoE Compression
124.one_line: Structured pruning, layer removal and mixture-of-experts compression to make large language models cheaper to store and serve.

125.name: Physical Plausibility in Video Generation
125.one_line: Evaluating and improving physical consistency, motion realism and world modeling in text-to-video generators.

126.name: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretability
126.one_line: Building, evaluating and stress-testing sparse autoencoders and dictionary learning to extract interpretable features from model activations.

127.name: Neural Combinatorial Optimization
127.one_line: Learned solvers, often diffusion or RL based, for routing, SAT, MILP and other constraint satisfaction problems.

128.name: EEG and Physiological Foundation Models
128.one_line: Foundation models, benchmarks and datasets for EEG, ECG and other physiological signals in clinical and brain-computer interface settings.

129.name: Human Motion and Gesture Generation
129.one_line: Generating, predicting and recognizing human motion, dance, gestures, gait and sign from text, scenes or video.

130.name: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Reasoning
130.one_line: Teacher-student distillation where reasoning LLMs learn from teacher feedback on their own generated trajectories.

131.name: Time Series Forecasting Models
131.one_line: Forecasting architectures and time series foundation models for multivariate, long-horizon and non-stationary data.

132.name: GraphRAG and RL-Trained Search Agents
132.one_line: Retrieval-augmented generation over knowledge graphs and RL-trained search agents for multi-hop question answering.

133.name: LLM Reasoning and Test-Time Scaling
133.one_line: Analyzing reasoning traces and reducing overthinking in large reasoning models through pruning, early stopping and search.

134.name: LLM RL Training Dynamics and Stability
134.one_line: Off-policy corrections, importance ratios, entropy control and credit assignment for stable reinforcement learning post-training of LLMs.

135.name: AI Governance, Position Papers and Human Oversight
135.one_line: Position and empirical papers on human oversight, AI-assisted decisions, governance and how AI systems should be evaluated with people.

136.name: Causal Identifiability and Latent-Variable Models
136.one_line: Learning causal graphs and identifying causal effects with structural causal models, interventions and latent variables.

137.name: Algorithmic Fairness and Group Constraints
137.one_line: Fair classification and regression, multigroup fairness, fairness audits and fairness-accuracy tradeoffs under sensitive attributes.

138.name: Robust Regression and Statistical Inference
138.one_line: Statistical theory for linear regression, covariance estimation and inference under heavy tails, corruption and high dimensions.

139.name: Tabular Foundation Models
139.one_line: In-context tabular foundation models such as TabPFN plus benchmarks, robustness, privacy and generation for tabular data.

140.name: Protein Language Models and Structure
140.one_line: Protein language models, structure prediction, docking and fitness prediction for biomolecules and drug discovery.

141.name: Bayesian and Multi-Objective Optimization
141.one_line: Sample-efficient black-box optimization with Gaussian process surrogates, acquisition functions and multi-objective Pareto search.

142.name: LLM Behavioral Tendencies and Evaluation Awareness
142.one_line: Evaluating LLM behaviors such as sycophancy, deception, confirmation bias, moral reasoning, risk attitudes and evaluation awareness.

143.name: Tool-Use, Web and GUI Agent Benchmarks
143.one_line: Benchmarks and evaluation suites for tool-using, web, GUI and professional-workflow language agents.

144.name: Speech and Audio Language Models
144.one_line: Large audio language models, speech recognition, speech enhancement, audio generation and sign language recognition.

145.name: LLM Hallucination and Uncertainty
145.one_line: Detecting and reducing hallucinations in LLMs and vision-language models using uncertainty, token-level signals and training.

146.name: Model Selection and Evaluation Pitfalls
146.one_line: Data-centric studies of benchmarks, model selection, cascades and evaluation pitfalls in how model behavior is measured.

147.name: Stochastic and Convex Optimization Theory
147.one_line: Convergence rates for stochastic, decentralized, minimax and nonconvex gradient methods, including heavy-tailed noise and step-size schedules.

148.name: Neural Network Verification and Backdoors
148.one_line: Formal verification and certified robustness of neural networks, plus backdoor attacks and provable defenses.

149.name: Clustering Coresets and Nearest Neighbor Search
149.one_line: Algorithms and guarantees for coresets, k-means and k-center clustering, metric spaces and approximate nearest neighbor search.

0.name: LLM Agents
0.one_line: Benchmarks, memory, skills, safety, multi-agent coordination and multi-turn training for tool-using and coding LLM agents, plus human oversight of AI decisions.

1.name: Vision & Perception
1.one_line: Feed-forward and Gaussian-splatting 3D reconstruction, 3D scene grounding, LiDAR perception, medical imaging, restoration, anomaly and OOD detection, and image forensics.

2.name: LLM Behavior & Safety
2.one_line: Interpretability, evaluation, sycophancy, hallucination, jailbreaks, unlearning, knowledge editing, steering and watermarking of language models, plus AI governance and position papers.

3.name: Optimization & Statistics
3.one_line: Optimizer design such as Muon and Adam, stochastic and convex convergence theory, robust regression, Bayesian optimization and neural combinatorial optimization.

4.name: Graph Learning & Recommendation
4.one_line: Graph neural network architectures, graph foundation models, generative models for graphs and hypergraphs, and sequential and generative recommendation.

5.name: DL Theory & Neuroscience
5.one_line: Learning dynamics and generalization theory, representation geometry, attribution and sparse autoencoders, plus brain decoding, spiking networks, quantum ML and verification.

6.name: Robotics & Embodied AI
6.one_line: Vision-language-action policies, dexterous and humanoid manipulation, autonomous driving, world models for planning and embodied spatial reasoning.

7.name: Vision-Language & Speech Models
7.one_line: Visual reasoning, image-text alignment, multimodal fusion, benchmarks and test-time adaptation for vision-language models, plus speech and audio language models.

8.name: LLM Reasoning & Retrieval
8.one_line: Efficient chain-of-thought, agentic reasoning, formal math and verified code, LLM-driven optimization modeling, clinical reasoning and retrieval-augmented generation.

9.name: Reinforcement Learning
9.one_line: Deep, offline, multi-agent, goal-conditioned and constrained RL, generative policies and convergence theory for MDPs.

10.name: Video Generation & Understanding
10.one_line: Long and controllable video generation, physical plausibility, long-video QA, temporal grounding and human motion generation.

11.name: Time Series & Forecasting
11.one_line: Time series forecasting models, irregular and continuous-time sequences, weather and climate prediction, and urban mobility.

12.name: Trustworthy & Statistical ML
12.one_line: Federated learning, differential privacy, fairness, conformal prediction, calibration, causal effect estimation, noisy labels, PAC theory, clustering and tabular foundation models.

13.name: LLM Post-Training
13.one_line: RL with verifiable rewards, preference optimization, reward models, on-policy distillation and continual learning for language models.

14.name: PDEs & Dynamical Systems
14.one_line: Neural operators, physics-informed networks and data-driven identification of dynamical systems.

15.name: Image & 3D Generation
15.one_line: Text-to-image generation and evaluation, efficient high-resolution diffusion, image editing, unified multimodal models, part-level 3D assets and concept erasure.

16.name: Bandits, Games & Mechanisms
16.one_line: Bandit regret and best-arm identification, online convex optimization, equilibrium learning in games, and mechanism design and social choice.

17.name: Diffusion, Flows & Inference
17.one_line: Diffusion guidance and sampling, flow matching, diffusion theory, optimal transport, and variational and simulation-based Bayesian inference.

18.name: Efficient LLMs & Architectures
18.one_line: Transformer theory, sparse attention, KV cache, quantization, pruning, speculative decoding, PEFT, model merging, scaling laws, diffusion language models and LLM-written GPU kernels.

19.name: Biomolecules & Causal Discovery
19.one_line: Single-cell, protein, molecule and chemistry models alongside causal discovery and structural causal models.
